scoringPolicy: One uniform engineering readiness rubric for every public Kingdom Index route. Each criterion requires an independently inspectable dated receipt for its scored points. Source inspection alone cannot certify browser, production performance or financial correctness.

criteria.requirement: Canonical database and external truth sources, identity and provenance validated against independent observations
Boundary cases, money/result invariants and permissions proven under realistic input
Malformed, absent, stale, partial and contradictory data fail safely without invented truth
Authentication, authorization, privacy and hostile-input paths independently exercised
Main workflows verified in production-equivalent conditions
Navigation, refresh, search, pagination and preference state maintain consistent semantics
Keyboard, focus, screen reader and reduced-motion behaviour verified
Mobile and desktop behavior plus loading, empty and failure states verified
Measured cold/warm navigation and P75/P95 performance on specified device/network budgets
Query plans, pagination, payload size and cache invalidation proven at production-scale row counts
Component rerenders, heap growth and JS footprint profiled under interactions
Concurrency and sustained usage within stated infrastructure budgets
Logic separated by stable domain contracts; no unnecessary coupling, duplication or giant state ownership
Transitive dependencies and source provenance tracked, including shared code and configuration
Canonical contracts, operator playbooks, limitations and change receipts current
New functionality can be added without violating tested interfaces or unrelated routes
Property, unit and adversarial tests cover correctness and failure modes
Real data/database and API integration boundaries exercised
Cold browser interaction, accessibility and visual/layout regression verified
Exact-source CI, staging, production and rollback evidence preserved

certification.rule: Score 100 requires all weighted criteria demonstrably satisfied on the exact deployed source, an independent production/browser performance receipt, and current provenance. Unknown evidence earns no points; tests passing alone never grant 100.
